title: Pseudoreplication and the Design of Ecological Field Experiments
notes: Canonical statement of the failure mode this repository independently rejected as REJ-COHORT-05: treating non-independent replicates as independent inflates the false-positive rate. The rejection of the N=40 pseudoreplicated cohort and the move to disjoint N=100 cohorts matches the standard remedy (independent experimental units). Cite as vindication of that decision, not as an endorsement of the analysis.

title: A Practitioner's Guide to Cluster-Robust Inference
authors: Cameron, A. C.; Miller, D. L.
notes: Supplies the correct inferential frame for the paired ablation design: seeds are clusters, and the paired within-seed contrast is the estimation target. Relevant caveat the repository does not currently state: with ~40-100 clusters the wild cluster bootstrap is preferred over the percentile bootstrap, and with fewer than ~10 clusters the six-point (Webb) weight distribution becomes necessary. Round 1 did not verify which bootstrap variant `AIEF_1_3_paired_statistics_updated.py` uses beyond its 95% percentile interval claim; that is a Round 2 audit item.

title: Nonlinear normal modes and spectral submanifolds: existence, uniqueness and use in model reduction
notes: Gives the precise sense in which REJ-SPEC-01 was doomed: an exact slow reduction requires an invariant manifold tangent to a spectral subspace, not a truncated POD basis. The rejected 8D compression assumed a finite-dimensional invariant subspace it never established. This is the strongest external justification for the REJ-SPEC-01 rejection in the current record.

title: Data-Driven Reduced Modeling of Delayed Dynamical Systems via Spectral Submanifolds
authors: Abbasciano, G.; Buza, G.; Haller, G.
notes: Highest-priority find of Round 1. This is the direct methodological competitor to the rejected POD compression and the correct framework for the AIEF-1.4 delay system: it reduces a DDE to a low-dimensional ODE model without knowing the delay structure, and reports predictive power retained under chaos. Two consequences. (1) REJ-SPEC-01 is not merely a coding error; a sound delay-aware reduction exists and was not attempted. (2) A future AIEF-1.4 spectral program has a published, citable target to reproduce or beat, instead of an internally invented baseline.

title: Data-driven discovery of Koopman eigenfunctions for control
authors: Kaiser, E.; Kutz, J. N.; Brunton, B. W.
notes: Names the closure/aliasing failure that produces plausible-looking but spurious eigenvalues in exactly the regime REJ-SPEC-01 occupied. Usable as the formal justification that an 8D projected operator's spectrum is not automatically attributable to the full system.

title: Avoiding spectral pollution for transfer operators using residuals
authors: Herwig, A.; Colbrook, M. J.; Junge, O.; Koltai, P.; Slipantschuk, J.
notes: Supplies the residual-based (ResDMD-style) acceptance test the rejected spectral program lacked: an eigenpair is only admissible if its residual against the full dynamics is small. This is directly implementable as a gate on any future slow-mode claim and would have caught REJ-SPEC-01 automatically. Round 2 action item: specify the residual threshold that AIEF-1.4 slow modes must satisfy.

title: Koopman Reduced Order Modeling with Confidence Bounds
authors: Mohr, R.; Fonoberova, M.; Mezic, I.
notes: The constructive alternative to the rejected compression: truncating the spectrum is only defensible if the discarded remainder is carried as an explicit error process with bounds. AIEF-1.4 truncation carried no such term, so 'faithfully captures' in REJ-SPEC-01 had no quantitative referent. Gives a template for stating a bounded claim instead of a qualitative one.

title: Spectra and Pseudospectra: The Behavior of Nonnormal Matrices and Operators
notes: Frames CAVEAT-MS-8.4 and CF08 correctly. When the finite-step operator is non-normal, left and right eigenvectors are not orthogonal and the pointwise left-covector decomposition is not an invariant object; it is a property of one fiber/eigenvector normalization. The draft Corollary 8.4 defect (the extra diag(x_G) C_G term) is the concrete instance. Round 2 action item: compute the pseudospectrum radius of the audited AIEF-1.4 operator at eps=1e-8 to state the tie-margin claim in Trefethen-Embree terms rather than as an ad hoc tolerance.

title: Optimization and Nonsmooth Analysis
notes: The map A_eps(x) = M(Ax)x with min()-selected endpoint winners is piecewise-smooth and generally not differentiable at winner ties, which is exactly the regime REJ-SPEC-02 and S04 (the t=124.05 'event') live in. Clarke's generalized gradient is the standard object of record there. This converts an unexplained sensitivity into a named mathematical condition: at a tie the branchwise Jacobian does not exist and a directional/generalized derivative must be reported instead.

title: Introduction to Functional Differential Equations
authors: Hale, J. K.; Verduyn Lunel, S. M.
notes: Formal license for the repository's central structural claim: for a delay system the state is the history segment x_t, so 'memory' is not an extra feature but part of the state space. This is why EMP-AIEF14-01 (reset_B is not a unique bottleneck) is unsurprising rather than paradoxical: removing one component of a history-dependent state leaves the history itself intact.

title: Algebraic Graph Theory
notes: Anchors LEAN-CF-01 in the literature. ker C_{2,7} = span{(1,-1,-1)} is the n-c instance for the 2-vertex/3-edge multigraph with c=1: rank = n - c = 1, so nullity = 3 - 1 = 2 in edge coordinates, and the Lean statement is the specific orientation-compatible computation. The Lean result is therefore a correct specialization of a classical theorem, which is the right status: formalized theorem, not new mathematics.

title: Parallel Reproducible Summation
notes: Bounds what IMPL-MODULAR-01 can honestly claim. Bit-identical agreement is a same-order, same-environment property; it is not guaranteed across architectures, compilers, libm versions or thread counts. The observed cross-host drift (4.405e-13 on continuous arrays, 0.0 on discrete P_* arrays) is the textbook behaviour, not a defect. IMPL-MODULAR-01 is correctly scoped to 'identical host/libm environment' already; this reference is what makes that scope boundary citable rather than merely cautious.

title: Algorithms for Efficient Reproducible Floating Point Summation
authors: Ahrens, W.; Demmel, J.; Nguyen, H. D.
notes: Actionable if the project ever wants cross-platform bitwise reproducibility rather than tolerance-gated reproducibility. Round 2/3 candidate: specify the two-tier tolerance gate for Stage 7 CI (0.0 on discrete P_* arrays; a justified absolute tolerance for continuous DDE arrays) and cite this as the reason a 0-ULP gate is not attainable by default.

title: What every computer scientist should know about floating-point arithmetic
notes: Baseline reference for two separate repo findings. (a) The eps=1e-8 finite-difference Jacobian in REJ-SPEC-02 is two to three orders of magnitude larger than the 4.44e-14 tie margins it was meant to resolve, so the reported spectrum is dominated by the difference step, not the dynamics. (b) The 4.405e-13 cross-host drift is at the rounding-error scale the tutorial predicts. Both are now citable rather than asserted.

title: Network Motifs: Simple Building Blocks of Complex Networks
authors: Milo, R.; Shen-Orr, S.; Itzkovitz, S.; Kashtan, N.; Chklovskii, D.; Alon, U.
notes: Defines the standard the rejected K3 census did not meet. 'Motif' is a statement about excess over a degree-matched null ensemble, never a raw count. REJ-K3-04 reported 856 K3 instances and inferred dominance; the correct comparison is against a configuration-model ensemble at matched degree sequence, and the audit already found only 26 isolated K3 components. Round 2 action item: specify the null model and rewiring count needed to restate any K3 claim as a z-score.

title: Network Attractors driven by Time-Delay Plasticity
authors: Ruschel, S.; Hristov, E.; Meijer, H. G. E.; Coombes, S.; Nicks, R.
notes: Closest published neighbour to the AIEF-1.4 memory/timescale programme: adaptive delays that reshape effective coupling, select frequencies, and stabilise network attractors. Two uses. (1) Priority/scoop risk: EMP-AIEF14-02 is a specific instance of a mechanism now under independent investigation, so the repository should state the novelty boundary explicitly (its contributions are the ablation design and the topological-recovery metric, not the existence of delay-driven frequency selection). (2) Benchmark: the AAD literature has an algebraic frequency-selection picture, which is a stricter standard than a numerically observed T_window sensitivity.
